Agentic Platform

What is MCP?

Model Context Protocol

An open standard (by Anthropic) for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources.

  • Standardized interface — one protocol, any tool
  • Server/Client model — tools are MCP servers, agents are clients
  • Discoverable — agents can browse available tools
  • Composable — mix and match tools from any provider

Example: Outlook MCP Server

1. Agent discovers tools tools/list

read_emails send_email search_inbox create_event

2. Agent reads tool schema

send_email
  desc: "Send an email via Outlook"
  inputs: to: string, subject: string, body: string

3. Agent calls the tool tools/call

send_email(to="alice@loreal.com",
  subject="Q3 Report", body="...")
→ {"status": "sent", "id": "msg-42"}

Agentic Platform

What is A2A?

Agent-to-Agent Protocol

An open standard (by Google) for agents to communicate and collaborate with each other.

  • Agent discovery — agents publish an Agent Card
  • Task delegation — one agent sends a task to another
  • Interoperable — works across frameworks & vendors
  • Complementary to MCP — MCP = tools, A2A = agents

Example: "Analyze Q3 sales in France"

1. Discover agents /.well-known/agent.json

Data Analyst Agent
  skills: "Query databases, generate charts"
  url: https://data-agent.loreal.com

2. Orchestrator sends task tasks/send

message: "Get Q3 2025 sales for France by brand"
→ status: "working"

3. Agent returns result

status: "completed"
artifact: {type: "text", data: "L'Oréal Paris: +12%..."}

Agent Theory

LLM vs. Agent

Classic LLM

Single pass: prompt → response

  • No access to external data
  • No ability to take actions
  • Knowledge frozen at training time
ReactiveStateless

Example:

User: "What are L'Oréal Q3 results?"

LLM: "I don't have access to recent financial data."

AI Agent

Multi-step: reason → act → observe → repeat

  • Reasons about what to do
  • Uses tools (search, APIs, databases...)
  • Loops until the task is complete
AutonomousTool-using

Same question:

1. Thinks: I need financial data → search_tool

2. Reads results → extracts key figures

3. Responds with accurate, sourced answer

Agent Theory

The ReAct Loop

Agents follow a Reasoning + Acting cycle:

User Question
→
THOUGHT
"What should I do?"
→
ACTION
Call a tool
→
OBSERVATION
Get the result
→
ANSWER

Example: "What's the weather in Paris?"

THOUGHT → ACTION: google_search("weather Paris") → OBSERVATION: "15°C" → ANSWER

Agent Theory

Agentic Frameworks

A framework that handles the plumbing so you focus on logic:

  • ReAct loop — automatic reasoning
  • Tool integration — any function or API
  • Session management — memory
  • Multi-agent orchestration
  • Tracing & debugging

Today we use Google ADK.

Agent Theory

Google ADK — Agent Development Kit

Core Concepts

ComponentRole
AgentLLM + instructions + tools
RunnerManages the ReAct loop
SessionConversation history
ToolFunction the agent can call

Minimal Agent

from google.adk.agents import Agent
from google.adk.tools import google_search

agent = Agent(
    name="my_agent",
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    instruction="You are a helpful assistant.",
    tools=[google_search],
)

google_search — real-time web search

Custom Tools

def get_stock_price(ticker: str) -> dict:
    """Get the current stock price.
    Args:
        ticker: Stock symbol (e.g. "AAPL")
    """
    return {"price": 185.50, "currency": "USD"}

How the Agent Uses Tools

1. Reads the docstring

2. Decides when to use it

3. Formats arguments

4. Framework executes & returns

RAG Theory

The Problem RAG Solves

Without RAG

  • LLM only knows training data
  • No private documents
  • Context window limited
  • Retraining expensive

With RAG

  • Retrieve relevant chunks
  • Augment the prompt
  • Generate informed answer
  • Always up-to-date
